name: cargo-show-asm
desc: Show assembly, LLVM-IR, MIR, and WASM generated for Rust code
why: Shows the assembly and LLVM-IR behind Rust code, useful for poking at compiler output, though a niche dev tool.

brief.what_it_is: cargo-show-asm is a Cargo subcommand (installed as cargo-asm) that displays the assembly, LLVM-IR, MIR, and WASM that rustc generates for Rust source code. You point it at a crate target (lib, bin, example, test, or bench) and optionally a function name. It runs the build, then prints the matching function's output in the chosen format. Output can be Intel or AT&T assembly, interleaved Rust source, llvm-ir, MIR, WASM, or llvm-mca analysis, and it can also emit a JSON list of functions.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a way to see the code rustc generates for any function, which is useful when you want to check what the compiler actually produced rather than guess from the source.
brief.how_it_works: Running cargo asm against a single focused target makes cargo-show-asm invoke rustc to produce an assembly file, then list the public functions it finds with their line counts. Passing a demangled name, a unique partial name, or an index selects one function and prints its code. Options such as --context N recursively pull in the bodies of called functions, and --callers-of takes a regex to filter functions by their call graph.

commands_seen.context: The README's install command, which builds it from crates.io.
Run with no parameters; the README says it will suggest how to narrow the search scope.

Narrow the listing to functions whose names contain the partial string from_.
Dump the full assembly for one fully named function.

List functions that call something matching panic, for finding code that can panic.
Generate bash shell completion; the README says to use cargo-asm rather than cargo asm for it to work. Zsh, fish, and elvish variants are also listed.
Install with the bright-color feature for colorful line parser output; a dull-color feature is also offered.

brief.install_notes: Installed through the Homebrew formula here, or with cargo install cargo-show-asm from crates.io. The --file option needs the binary compiled with the disasm feature. The --wasm output needs the wasm32-unknown-unknown target installed. Shell completion is generated by the cargo-asm binary and placed into the shell's completion directory by hand. No accounts or external services are mentioned.
brief.standout: It shows compiler output for a specific function, filters by call graph (for example, every function that can reach panic), and can interleave Rust source with assembly. It covers several IR stages (asm, LLVM-IR, MIR, WASM, llvm-mca) in one tool, where many alternatives cover only one.
brief.status: unknown. The README is detailed and current-looking: it covers stable and nightly Rust, and it links to rust-lang PR 116505 and to issue 247. However, the fetched page shows no release date, version number, or last-commit date, so I cannot confirm recent maintenance.
brief.caveats: Platform support is Linux and macOS, with limited Windows support. The default build is --release, and --dev has to be passed explicitly. Functions may not appear if rustc does not generate them: generic functions need a concrete wrapper, and small functions may be inlined, so the README suggests #[inline(never)]. --file needs the disasm feature. --wasm needs the wasm32-unknown-unknown target. The project is dual-licensed under Apache-2.0 or MIT. The brew formula reported no caveats.
quotes: A cargo subcommand that displays the Assembly, LLVM-IR, MIR and WASM generated for Rust source code.
Show the code rustc generates for any function

`rustc` will only generate the code for your function if it knows what type it is, including generic parameters and if it is exported (in case of a library) and not inlined (in case of a binary, example, test, etc.).
